verdict: 2026-07-24 18:14:48 PDT — The slice-first pipeline and fail-closed posture are directionally sound, but I would not build the cross-cutting harness from this sketch yet. Its verification join cannot actually refute an identified claim, its coverage model classifies successful negative sweeps as uncovered, and its fan-out does not realize the plan's deep-run cardinality. I would retain the Workflow-based pipeline but drive it from an explicit run manifest, use claim-independent evidence records for adversarial verification, and model execution coverage separately from finding outcomes.

findings.title: A claim-blind verifier cannot refute a specific finding
findings.locus: Design sketch — HOW, stage 4: Adversarial verify
findings.claim: The verifier receives only file:line and never the finding's claim, yet must decide whether that finding was refuted. Location alone provides no proposition to test and no typed join between the verifier's observation and the finder finding. The mechanical-confirmation example itself needs to know that the alleged behavior is “this catch swallows,” exposing the missing input. As sketched, implementations must either leak the claim through another channel or treat independent rediscovery near the same line as verification; neither supplies the promised precision guarantee.
findings.alternative: Keep the verifier claim-blind but have it emit a structured, claim-independent evidence record for the cited location and lens: observable control flow, error propagation behavior, reachable outcomes, and uncertainty. Then apply a deterministic adjudication step that evaluates the stored finder claim against those facts. Define stable finding/evidence IDs and the exact promote/refute decision table as part of the reusable verifier contract.
findings.win: Eliminates an undefined judgment handoff and prevents nearby-but-different defects from falsely corroborating a finder. The same evidence/adjudication contract can serve every future lens without covertly weakening context asymmetry.

findings.title: Coverage and finding outcomes are collapsed into one set
findings.locus: Design sketch — HOW, stage 5: Synthesis + coverage accounting
findings.claim: The proposed `notCovered` union includes scheduled rows with zero surviving findings. Such a row was covered and produced a negative result; it was not omitted. Encoding it as uncovered conflates execution coverage with defect yield, contradicts the sketch's own failure-versus-omission invariant, and makes a clean audit indistinguishable from a scope gap in the canonical report contract future lenses will inherit.
findings.alternative: Use a declarative per-row execution ledger with distinct states such as planned, executed, omitted, and failed, plus `verifiedFindingCount`. Generate `notCovered` only from planned omissions and out-of-slice scope; list executed rows with zero survivors under covered execution. Continue suppressing the entire report on any failed row.
findings.win: Centralizes the coverage invariant, removes ambiguous set arithmetic, and makes zero-defect sweeps, intentional omissions, and fatal execution failures mechanically distinguishable without prose interpretation.

findings.title: Fan-out does not encode deep-run multiplicity
findings.claim: The plan contract defines a deep row as `runs = 2 × |unitIds|`, but the Workflow fans out once over `unitIds`. Deep rows contain the same full unit list as standard rows, so depth is not actually “baked into unitIds”; iterating that list launches only half the approved and priced deep runs. “At the row's depth” does not define what the second run is or how its output and provenance join.
findings.alternative: Materialize one declarative execution manifest before spawning: expand every row into run records keyed by row identity, unitId, and pass index, with the pass count derived from the depth factor. Validate that manifest cardinality and estimated cost equal the approved plan, then have Workflow map exactly those records and aggregate them by row/unit.
findings.win: Eliminates bespoke depth handling in the orchestrator, makes the launched fleet equal the approved price and schedule by construction, and gives every finder artifact an unambiguous run identity for failure accounting and verification provenance.
